result:
Okay, I'll take you up on that.

I want to write about the quiet things.

Not the big, loud moments - not birthdays or graduations or rockets launching. I mean the quiet things that happen in between, that no one ever claps for but that actually make up 99% of being alive.

Like the way light looks at 4:47pm on a random Tuesday. It's not sunset yet, it's not quite afternoon. It comes in sideways through a window and turns dust in the air into slow-moving galaxies. And for a second your entire room looks like it's underwater.

Or the secret life of everyday objects. Your favorite mug knows more about you than most people do. It knows how you hold it when you're tired versus when you're just cold. It knows you tap the side of it twice before you drink. It has been there for bad news and good news and boring news and no news at all.

I think about how every person is an archive.

You walk past someone on the street and you're passing an entire library. They have a song that immediately makes them 14 again. They have a scar with a story they've gotten tired of telling. They have a joke that only three people in the world would understand, and one of those people maybe doesn't talk to them anymore. And you'll never know any of it. You'll just see them for two seconds while you both wait for the crosswalk to change.

That's kind of heartbreaking and kind of beautiful at the same time.

Maybe that's why we look up at the sky so much. The stars are the opposite of that - they are so distant and so public. Everyone on Earth has seen the same moon. It's the one thing we all definitely share. You can be lonely in a city of eight million people, but you can look up and know that someone else, somewhere else, maybe someone you miss, is looking at that same little white circle and thinking similar thoughts.

I like to think the universe isn't really made of atoms. It's made of small, noticed moments.

The moment you remember a word that was on the tip of your tongue for hours. The moment a dog decides to sit right on your foot for no reason. The moment you overhear a kid explaining something with complete, absolute confidence and getting it totally wrong.

If we paid more attention, we'd realize we are surrounded by miracles that are just very, very quiet.

So that's what I wanted to write about. The quiet miracles.

What's a quiet little moment you've noticed lately that stuck with you for some reason?
